summary: In this presentation, Ado Kukic of Sourcegraph introduces the Code AI Maturity Model, a framework designed to benchmark the progress of AI in software development, drawing a parallel to the SAE levels of driving autonomy. Kukic notes that 92% of developers now use AI code tools, up from 1% a year ago, and cites a prediction by Sourcegraph CEO Quinn Slack that 99% of code will be AI-written within five years. The model consists of six distinct levels categorized into human-initiated, AI-initiated, and AI-led stages. Level 0 represents traditional manual coding. Level 1 involves AI generating single lines or blocks based on developer intent, akin to cruise control. Level 2 provides superior context-aware suggestions specific to the codebase, comparable to partial driving automation. Level 3 shifts to AI delivering full code solutions and integrations from high-level requirements, with the AI acting as the primary driver and the human as a fallback. Level 4 introduces proactive AI that autonomously monitors changes and bug reports to submit pull requests without developer oversight, mirroring highly automated taxis like Waymo. Finally, Level 5 grants AI complete autonomy over the software development lifecycle, from design to deployment, requiring only high-level human validation of the end product, similar to fully autonomous vehicles under all conditions. The talk concludes with a promotion for Sourcegraph's AI assistant, Cody.

takeaways: The Code AI Maturity Model defines six levels of AI coding assistance across three categories: human-initiated, AI-initiated, and AI-led.
The model is explicitly compared to the SAE levels of driving autonomy to illustrate the progression of AI control.
Adoption of AI code tools has surged from 1% to 92% of developers over the past year.
Levels 0-2 focus on human-initiated tasks, scaling from manual coding to context-aware completions.
Levels 3-4 represent AI-initiated actions, where AI builds full components from requirements or proactively submits pull requests.
Level 5 describes an AI-led future where AI handles the entire software development lifecycle with minimal human guidance.
Sourcegraph builds Cody, an AI coding assistant designed to understand a user's entire codebase.

sections.title: Levels 0-2: Human-Initiated AI
sections.summary: Details Level 0 (manual coding), Level 1 (AI generates single lines/blocks based on intent), and Level 2 (AI uses specific codebase context for superior completions), comparing them to SAE Levels 0-2.

sections.title: Levels 3-4: AI-Initiated Coding
sections.summary: Explains Level 3 (AI builds full components from high-level requirements) and Level 4 (AI proactively monitors code and bugs to submit PRs), mapped to SAE Levels 3-4.

sections.title: Level 5 and Conclusion
sections.summary: Describes Level 5 (AI handles the entire software development lifecycle with minimal human validation) and concludes with a call to visit Sourcegraph's booth and try Cody.

limitations: At Level 3, AI may encounter situations where it cannot perform tasks and must give control back to the human developer.
Level 4 AI operates under specific conditions rather than universally.
